title: Check yourself: Why long explorations degrade, and where their findings should live

questions.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. After two hours on a payments codebase, the agent answers a question about retries by describing how such systems typically retry, though it read the actual retry classes an hour earlier. Which practice would have prevented this?

options.text: Writing specific findings to a notes file and consulting it for later queries
options.says: The specifics are kept in a file that outlives the window and are read again when a later question needs them.

options.text: Switching to a model with a bigger context window for the whole of the session
options.says: Ruled out because "a bigger window only moves the problem later".

options.text: Raising the output limit so that each answer can quote more of the code
options.says: Ruled out because the symptom is that "answers become inconsistent from one turn to the next, and specific names give way to plausible generalities", which more output does not repair.

options.text: Telling the agent in its prompt to avoid generic answers from here onward
options.says: Ruled out because "A reminder in the prompt does not bring back a class that has left the window".

origin.section: What a filled context looks like

questions.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A coordinator must list every test file that covers refunds in a very large repository, then trace the refund flow. It does both in its own conversation, and the context fills with listings and file contents. Which structure fits?

options.text: Hand the whole job to one helper with the brief to explore everything and report it all
options.says: Ruled out because "a broad brief returns a broad report".

options.text: Keep the reading in the coordinator and add a notes file for what it finds
options.says: Ruled out because "Each file read, each search result, each command output stays in the window", so the coordinator's own reading keeps filling it.

options.text: Give each question to a read-only exploring helper and keep just the summaries
options.says: Each narrow question goes to a read-only subagent, and the coordinator receives only a summary.

options.text: Use a helper with every tool, so that it can save the lists to files
options.says: Ruled out because "Read-only matters: an exploration that can edit can also damage".
